clue.text: Venomous creature with nemesis for Cleopatra?

parts.note: Cleopatra died from the bite of an asp, a small Egyptian snake

explanation.surface: A deadly animal is linked with the snake that killed the Egyptian queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and the asp are both venomous, so the surface seems to describe one creature twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasp carries a stinging venom, so it counts as a poisonous creature.

clue.text: Turn to go down to Tube — one should take in the air

definitions.text: one should take in the air

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part goes above, going down to the second

parts.note: to wind is to turn, as with a clock key
a pipe is a tube

explanation.surface: A trip down to the London Underground for fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' suggests the London Underground, but it is just a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea carries breathed air down to the lungs.

clue.text: Hat must be raised or placed at foot of grave

indicators.note: in a down clue the reversed word sits below, at the foot of the other

parts.note: sombre means grave or serious

indicators.note: raised means turned upwards, so in a down clue the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hat is lifted or left at the foot of a tombstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be raised' turns OR into RO; 'grave' looks like a burial site but means serious.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a wide-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: During race, say, fences left unfinished

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: fences means encloses, so the competing word surrounds the letter for left

parts.note: to race is one example of how to compete

explanation.surface: Fences put up along a racecourse were left half-built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fences' looks like the jumps on a racecourse, but it is a verb here: COMPETE encloses L to give COMPLETE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left unfinished is not whole or ended, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Almost comes to, hearing organ in different directions

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: N and S, north and south, are two different compass directions
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Someone nearly regains consciousness, ears pointing every which way.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach is to come close to, which is almost reaching.

clue.text: Broadcast Poe's gripping verse — about fifty fail to be stirred?

indicators.note: gripping means holding inside
broadcast means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name of Edgar Allan Poe; the 's is a link

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for verse surrounds the numeral

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Reading out a Poe poem fails to rouse about fifty listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred' means woken from sleep, not emotionally moved; 'Poe's gripping' reads as the 's being a link before the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeping too long means failing to wake on time, playing on stirred as roused.

clue.text: One may be depressed when in distress

definitions.text: One may be depressed when in distress

parts.words: One may be depressed when in distress
parts.note: depressed means pressed down, as an alarm is in an emergency, not feeling low

explanation.surface: Someone could feel low when troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depressed' reads as sad but means physically pushed.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency alarm is a switch pushed in a crisis.

clue.text: Overtake roughly in British river, lapping over another going north

indicators.note: in means placed inside the river letters
the two rivers overlap, sharing one letter, so the last letter of the first is written once

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means read upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: another river, the Dee
C, circa, means roughly

explanation.surface: A boat passes another in a British river, one flowing north.
explanation.walkthrough: The two rivers overlap, sharing a single E where they meet, before the abbreviation for circa is placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed is to go beyond, as overtaking goes past.

clue.text: Regular supporting the Spanish team

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means placed below the other piece

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
even means regular or uniform

explanation.surface: A loyal fan backs the Spanish side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular' looks like a person, a regular, but it means even.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football side has that many players, so the number stands for a team.

clue.text: Celebrity needs unlimited cover for teeth

indicators.note: without limits, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: enamel is the hard outer coating of teeth

explanation.surface: A famous person must have veneers fitted over their teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' strips E and L, the outer letters of ENAMEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A big name is a well-known person, so the word stands for fame or a famous figure.

clue.text: A celebrant converted in place of worship

indicators.note: changed in form, so the letters are rearranged; it also plays on religious conversion

explanation.surface: Someone leading a service has found religion in a chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' suggests religious conversion, fitting the church picture, but it signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabernacle is a building or tent used for religious meetings, a kind of house of worship.

clue.text: Demonstrations from the French led by trooper

indicators.note: the French word comes after, led by the soldier

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
des is French for 'of the' or 'from the'

explanation.surface: Displays from French forces are headed by a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Parades are public marches, which can be political protests or shows.

clue.text: Tame party with this person in charge — had a bite across street

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: across means stretching over, so the two pieces sit either side of the abbreviation

parts.note: me is how the setter refers to themselves
ate means had a bite

explanation.surface: At a quiet party, the host grabbed a snack over the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To domesticate an animal is to tame it.

clue.text: Hide in corner of a Greek island

parts.note: SE, the south-east, is one corner of a map
Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: Someone takes cover in a remote part of a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide in corner' reads as one instruction, but 'Hide' is the definition and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it, an exact synonym of hide as a verb.

clue.text: Harbour staff reported tug in case that's needed on voyage?

parts.note: a port is a harbour
to man something is to staff it

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word for tug is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to tow is to tug along

explanation.surface: Harbour workers said a tugboat was needed for a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: TEAU sounds like 'tow'.
explanation.definitionFit: A portmanteau is a large travelling bag that opens in two halves, the kind of luggage taken on a voyage.

clue.text: Of necessity, fuelled convertible in US city

indicators.note: in means placed inside the city's letters

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: convertible means able to be changed, so the letters are rearranged; it also suggests a soft-top car

explanation.surface: A fuelled-up soft-top car is driving in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convertible' looks like a car but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means necessarily, as must happen.

clue.text: What painter might have done the decks at sea?

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship's painter might have painted the decks on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'painter' is also a boat's rope, adding to the nautical picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist drafting a picture makes rough drawings.

clue.text: Oddly posey son, following fashionable prophets

indicators.note: following means coming after the other piece
oddly means the odd-numbered letters are taken

parts.note: chic means fashionable

explanation.surface: A pretentious son trails after trendy fortune-tellers.
explanation.definitionFit: People claiming to foresee the future are seers, like prophets.

clue.text: Side's leader laments wins becoming draws

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: weeps means laments
takes means wins, as in takes the prize

explanation.surface: A team's captain mourns that victories are turning into tied games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draws' looks like tied matches in a sports picture, but it means lotteries.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweepstake is a lottery-style prize draw, so these are draws in the sense of raffles.

clue.text: Major forces Right to go in union with extra trouble and strife?

definitions.text: union with extra trouble and strife?

indicators.note: 'to go' means must leave, so the letter for right departs from the military phrase

parts.note: a big army is a major force

explanation.surface: Large armed forces lose the right to join a union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble and strife' is Cockney rhyming slang for wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying again while still married means having an extra spouse.

clue.text: Going up in Dorset, a balloonist has a fall

indicators.note: Going up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A balloonist in Dorset rises and then comes down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden run SETABA, which 'Going up' reverses in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen or subside is to drop in intensity, as a storm dies down.

clue.text: Wearing pants, not quite sticking to the vital parts

parts.note: in means wearing, as in 'in a suit'

indicators.note: not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: briefs are underpants

explanation.surface: Someone in underwear only just covers their private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vital parts' suggests the body, but it means the essentials of an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking concisely means keeping only to the essential points, a summary.

clue.text: 'Insect from Outer Space' said to be crazy

indicators.note: said means spoken aloud, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a tick from the moon would be a lunar tick

explanation.surface: A sci-fi film title about a bug from space is called mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lunar tick' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A madman is a person who is mad, and the noun is used adjectivally to mean wildly insane.

clue.text: Grub is hot stuff — run to tuck in

indicators.note: to tuck in means to insert inside

parts.note: lava is molten rock, very hot stuff
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: The food is spicy — rush to eat it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' and 'tuck in' suggest food, but grub is an insect young.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is the young form of an insect.

clue.text: Constables perhaps assembled here, needing nerve to occupy big vessel

indicators.note: to occupy is to sit inside, so the word for nerve goes inside

parts.note: an artery is a major blood vessel
gall means nerve or cheek

explanation.surface: Police officers gather on a large ship, needing courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constables' looks like police, but means paintings by John Constable, the English landscape artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery is where paintings such as Constables are collected and shown.

clue.text: From an Asian land that lacks a border with India

indicators.note: losing an edge, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A country in Asia has no frontier with India.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something coming from Thailand, the Asian country.

clue.text: Confused East Rye with Rye in the past

indicators.note: mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone muddled East Rye with Rye some time ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Rye is an old town in East Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means in times gone by, the past.

clue.text: Creative works from Puerto de Santiago

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Artistic works come from a town in the Canary Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems, a kind of creative writing.
